content.body:
The Bell Model 14A was the first export version of the P-39 Airacobra. A mid-engine design and quick controls gave the P-39 a fairly unstable flight profile and earned it a reputation as a hot ship with a quick temper. While anemic at higher altitudes, it was very fast in low-level flight and practically unmatchable in a dive. France ordered hundreds of these at the same time they ordered the P-38 and P-40 designs under various export sales programs prior to their eventual surrender late in 1940.
With a single centerline mounted 20 mm cannon, and two .50 cal machinesguns in the cowling, plus four .303 cal guns in the wings, the Iron Dog carried more than enough firepower to handle a dogfight, but its delicate performance regime proved difficult to handle for most USAAF combat pilots. This limerick was penned by USAAF fighter pilots early in the Airacobra's deployment:
"...Don't give me a P-39 The engine is mounted behind She'll tumble and spin And she'll auger you in Don't give me a P-39"
On lend lease to Russian pilots the P-39 found its true home though, and it excelled so well in Eastern front combat operations that Russian orders kept the Airacobra production going almost single-handedly. Many Russian aces were made flying it. Speed and dive are the Airacobra's strong points, and with the 200 kg centerline bomb mount it makes a devastating ground support fighter.
Stay fast in the combat zone and do not attempt to mix it up with 109s. You stand a good chance against the Fw 190 if the fight is kept to the fast rolling style of fight, but be warned that heavy maneuvering is not the Iron Dog's strong point, and you can quickly find yourself face to face with the reputation behind that airman's little limerick.
